decision: Keep the original as default; the vectorization is verified-correct and 4.6% faster but does not justify changing the objective's core path for a claim-bearing run. At 52.87 examples/s an epoch is 45 min and $0.82, so the pilot is affordable without further optimization. If throughput becomes binding, profile inside the model with torch.profiler rather than guessing again.
diagnosis_was_wrong: The prediction was that backward would fall from ~500 ms to tens of ms because the per-alias Python loops generate thousands of tiny autograd nodes. Collapsing those into a handful moved backward by 2%. The alias loop was therefore NOT the dominant backward cost. Backward is 5.1x forward, which is unusual, so the remaining ~490 ms is inside _factorized_action_probability_tables (GNN encode and the per-family action-table heads) -- the batched part, which is unprofiled. The batch-scaling evidence (backward 14.3x for 4x batch) is real but has another cause.
speed_caveat: CPU shows no speedup, but CPU is not where the cost was: on A10G backward is 79% of the step because thousands of tiny autograd nodes each cost a kernel launch, which CPU does not pay. This implementation also still does O(aliases) Python work building index lists. Whether the reduced node count wins must be measured ON GPU.
tolerance_note: A segmented logsumexp reassociates the sum, so bitwise equality is not expected. The observed differences are float32 epsilon on the aggregated quantities and ~1e-8 on gradients; every unaggregated output is exactly equal.
